title: The first task
prompt: Which is the best first task for a new agent user?

setup.text: First real session. I have an hour, a project I care about, and I want to come out of this trusting the agent more, not less.

options.label: Change one homepage headline, leave styling alone, run the existing build, and show the diff.

outcome.text: Done. One file changed, the build passes, and here is the diff: the old headline out, your new one in. Nothing else touched.
I can read the whole change in ten seconds, and undoing it would be one step. Next time I’ll hand over something bigger.

options.verdict: The scope is narrow, the change is reversible, and both the build and the diff give you something concrete to inspect.

options.label: Modernize the whole application and clean up anything else you notice.

outcome.text: I updated 43 files: newer syntax, two library upgrades, some renamed components, and formatting cleanup along the way.
The site looks different and I can’t tell which of the 43 files mattered. If something broke, I wouldn’t know where to start looking.

options.verdict: The agent must invent the scope and the taste standard. “Anything else” also gives a small task permission to spread everywhere.

options.label: Rotate the production credentials and deploy them everywhere.

outcome.text: That touches your live accounts. If a step goes wrong, real users are locked out immediately, and there is no simple undo. I’d save this until we have a recovery plan.
Right. That one stays with me until I know how we’d recover.

options.verdict: It is concrete, but the cost of a mistake is too high for a first session. Start where recovery is cheap.
